label: echoed x input in copy phase (not the first copied token)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the token fed back as input is the letter x (essentially 100% of activation mass is on in_tok == x). It never fires during the original phase or at <DEL>, so original-phase x inputs do not trigger it. It is almost silent when x is the first copied token (recall_idx 1, i.e. orig(0) == x being fed back). The firing rate on echoed x rises with t and with sequence length: short sequences (L = 3-4) and early copy steps (t <= 7) often stay silent, and these account for most false positives. The strongest activations are on echoed x late in long sequences (L = 7-9), often the last copied input. Magnitude does not depend on the token being output or on digit counts. Dev F1 is 0.86 (precision 0.76, recall 0.995). Adding L >= 5 only raises F1 to 0.865.

issues: The explanation is wrong to say short sequences (L 3-4) and early copy steps 'account for most false positives'. On dev the predicate has about 18.0k false positives. L<=4 contributes about 3.4k (5419 predicted, precision 0.364) and recall_idx==2 about 5.3k (16647 predicted, precision 0.680). The slice outside both, L>=5 & recall_idx>=3, still has about 10.8k false positives (55002 predicted, precision 0.804), which is roughly 60% of the total.

'Firing rate rises with t and with sequence length' is only roughly true. Precision by L is 0.04, 0.39, 0.75, 0.83, 0.78, 0.76, 0.81 for L=3..9, so it is not monotone above L=5. Precision by recall_idx peaks at 4 (0.85) and drops at 6-7 (0.70-0.73). The firing rate per t plateaus after t of about 11.

The remaining ~20% non-firing on echoed x (L>=5) looks like diffuse noise rather than a systematic class. No simple variable separates it: prev_tok digit/letter/vowel/x, in_count, n_digits, next_out, first_tok, n_seen(x) and t parity all give precision between 0.73 and 0.81. to_go==0 (last step) is lower at 0.65, which slightly tempers the 'strongest on the last copied input' remark: top magnitudes are there, but the firing rate is lowest there.

The core claims hold. 100% of activation mass is in the copy phase, nothing fires in the original phase or at <DEL>, mass on in_tok x is 1.000, recall_idx 1 is nearly silent (272 active steps), there is no out_tok or digit-count dependence, and the predicate's test F1 is 0.859 (L>=5 variant: test F1 0.864). Misses are tiny (0.1% of mass), mostly weak firing on the first copied x at recall_idx 1.
